title: A map that is C¹ on an open set agrees near any of its points with a globally C¹ map (bump-function cut-off)
statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ, let V ⊆ ℝ^m be open, let ψ : ℝ^m → ℝ^P be of class C¹ on V (ContDiffOn ℝ 1 ψ V), and let v₀ ∈ V. Then there are a map g : ℝ^m → ℝ^P of class C¹ on all of ℝ^m (ContDiff ℝ 1 g) and a radius ρ > 0 such that the open ball B_ρ(v₀) is contained in V and g = ψ on B_ρ(v₀). Here ℝ^k = Euclid k with the Euclidean norm.
lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (V : Set (Euclid m)) (ψ : Euclid m → Euclid P) (v₀ : Euclid m), IsOpen V → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 ψ V → v₀ ∈ V → ∃ (g : Euclid m → Euclid P) (ρ : ℝ), 0 < ρ ∧ ball v₀ ρ ⊆ V ∧ ContDiff ℝ 1 g ∧ EqOn g ψ (ball v₀ ρ)
